claim: Novelty and value are separate targets: in one domain, patents that start a new topic get about 1.4x the citations, but fewer than 1% of patents are both novel and top-5% cited (20 of 189 novel patents in the top 5%).
agent_test: Score candidates on separate novelty and expected-value rubrics at equal tokens; check how often the top-novelty pick is also the top-value pick.

claim: Wide recombination (distant or diverse sources) has a direct citation benefit but a negative path through novelty, so the total effect is near zero (distance +0.211 direct, -0.129 indirect, total 0.082 ns). Novelty came from local deep search.
agent_test: Compare an agent forced to draw analogies from distant domains against one that digs deep in the home domain, same tokens, scoring novelty and value separately.

claim: The best-cited work is mostly conventional with a small tail of atypical combinations (9.11 hits per 100 vs 5 background; neither 2.05). Conventional core plus a dose of novelty beats either alone.
agent_test: Seed generation with one conventional anchor plus one atypical source vs all-atypical vs all-conventional; judge by blinded value ratings.

claim: Teams insert atypical combinations into a familiar base more often than solo authors (high tail novelty 36.1/39.8/49.7%; 37.7% higher for teams).
schema_part: none (multi-agent is out of scope for a single agent)
agent_test: Not directly testable for a single agent; could test several sampled personas merged into one idea pool.

claim: LLM-agent research ideas are rated more novel than expert human ideas in blind review (novelty 5.64 vs 4.84; with rerank 5.81), with no significant feasibility gain; idea stage, NLP only.
agent_test: Replicate on our tasks: LLM ideas vs human ideas, blind ratings. All lines come from one study.

claim: The idea-stage novelty advantage of LLM ideas does not survive execution: after 100+ hours of work AI ideas dropped 1.05 novelty and 1.88 effectiveness points, human ideas about 0; rankings flipped on most metrics (N=43).
agent_test: Require a cheap execution or test step before an idea is ranked; compare ranking from paper-stage scores to post-test scores.

claim: LLM idea generation saturates: 4,000 seed ideas reduce to about 200 after deduplication; LLM proposals cluster and are separable from human ones at 93-94% accuracy; different models give similar answers. Newer tests (2026) show the wall can be pushed back by structure: plan-then-split sampling or a coherence-minus-availability sampler give several times more distinct ideas, but refinement loops pull ideas back to one topic.
agent_test: At equal tokens, compare one long sample run against many short diverse-prompted runs; measure distinct ideas after dedup at cosine 0.8.

claim: LLMs are near chance at judging idea quality against expert ratings (43-53% against a 50% baseline), though expert agreement is itself only 56.1%. LLM reviewers match the weak human signal on accept/reject (65% vs 66%).
agent_test: Measure agreement of the agent's own ranking with held-out outcome labels; compare self-rank to random and to a pairwise-tournament rank.

claim: Fine-tuned or retrieval-augmented predictors can beat zero-shot LLMs and experts at predicting which idea works empirically (77.0% vs 51.4% zero-shot; experts 48.9% on 45 pairs), but benchmark outcomes are not long-run impact.
agent_test: Needs training data, so not a scaffold-only lever. Test zero-shot pairwise selection with evidence retrieval on our own task pairs.

claim: A large share of LLM 'novel' research proposals borrow from existing papers (24.0% verified plagiarism, 36% including unverified; 4% fully original; N=50, 13 experts). Automated checkers fail without the source paper.
agent_test: Run a retrieval-based prior-art check on each candidate and measure how many are dropped; compare to no check.

claim: Iterative retrieve-and-revise loops raise rated novelty but not technical depth (SciMON: 55.6% more novel after iteration 1; original paper idea judged better in 85% of comparisons); Nova reports 3.4x more unique ideas, judged largely by LLMs.
agent_test: Run revise-against-prior-art loops at equal tokens and score depth separately from novelty; avoid LLM-only judging.

claim: Text-only measures of 'different from the past, like the future' predict later citations (median to 90th percentile: +0.7 citations in 5 years on a median of 2) and can flag breakthroughs without citation data.
agent_test: Use an embedding-based past-vs-future novelty score on candidate ideas against a prior-art corpus; check against held-out impact.

claim: Predicting future high-impact concept pairs works on network features (AUC above 0.9), but experts rated LLM ideas from high-impact-predicted pairs low (mean 2.40/5; predicted-impact pairs 2.350 vs random 2.446), and interest fell as popularity rose.
agent_test: Do not use popularity or impact priors alone as a selector; test against interest ratings.

claim: Disruption-index findings (small teams disrupt, remote teams disrupt less, science getting less disruptive) rest on a measure with known artefacts. A reanalysis found the Park et al. decline comes from zero-reference records (97% of CD5=1 papers); the measure is time- and reference-count-sensitive. Original authors replied in Nature (2026) and say the decline holds on the critics' own data; no neutral adjudication read, so it stays contested.
agent_test: Do not use disruption-index results as design evidence for the schema.

claim: Disruption scores correlate only with some kinds of novelty (methods vs theory disagree across two studies) and not with peer-review ratings; reviewers do not agree well on novelty either.
agent_test: Not testable on an agent directly; treat as a warning about measurement.

claim: Generative AI help raises individual story novelty and usefulness (+6.7%, +6.4%) but makes outputs more similar to each other (5.2% closer to the AI idea), so collective novelty falls.
agent_test: Measure pairwise similarity across independent runs of the agent with and without an AI-idea seed.

claim: The tension view (go far) and the foundational view (go deep) are complementary: deep knowledge is needed to find the anomaly, wide search to raise mean value; inventor experience is the one control that helps both novelty and value.
agent_test: Test an agent given deep domain retrieval first, then far analogies, versus the reverse order, at equal tokens.

claim: Rare high-impact outputs have heavy tails: the mean is dominated by few outliers (novel patents mean 22.17 citations, range 0-187), so selection by average score loses them and seeing them needs large samples.
agent_test: Keep a small reserve of low-rated but atypical candidates through selection; measure whether tail wins appear.

claim: Homogenisation continues through execution: in an autoresearch loop, Claude ideas centred on interpretability rose from 2/10 ideas to 8/10 final reports, while ideas sampled by a coherence-minus-availability sampler stayed at 0/10; the sampler also had the best mean rank (0.633 vs 0.574 Claude, 0.295 random).
agent_test: Track topic concentration of ideas before and after the refine loop; add a distance-from-already-proposed penalty at selection.

claim: Diversity can be bought cheaply by structure: one planning call that proposes 5 directions and splits the sample across them raised mean pairwise distance by 0.13-0.25 over independent sampling at about 1.6x tokens (GPT-5.4), far more than the instruction 'be diverse' (0.04-0.06 at about 1.1x). Tested on creative-writing tasks only.
agent_test: Compare plan-then-split with plain repeated sampling at equal tokens on our own tasks; count distinct ideas after dedup.

claim: Chain-of-thought plus sampled personas raises idea diversity of a single LLM toward human level (persona+CoT 248 vs human 197 unique combinations on the full sample; bootstrap 65.4 vs 59.7). Ordinary sampled personas raised between-run spread more (0.635) than 'creative entrepreneur' ones (0.429).
agent_test: Use sampled ordinary personas, not 'be creative' roles, as a diversity operator; measure unique ideas.

claim: Cross-domain forcing helps humans' originality but gives strong LLMs no average gain (o3 and Claude Sonnet 4 b=0.02); it helps only on the most distant pairs (top 10% distance b=0.24). Originality trades off against feasibility (r=-0.74), and investment-worthiness follows utility, not originality.
schema_part: O (analogy) with gate on distance and a feasibility check
agent_test: Gate analogy seeds by embedding distance; rate feasibility separately; check whether the far-seed gain survives.

claim: Retrieval-grounded novelty checking works only with a facet-aware re-rank: on known not-novel ideas the full pipeline caught 89.7% vs 13.8% for general re-rank, 10.3% for embedding only, 5.2% for keyword only (n=58; test set 32 ideas, accuracy 0.81, kappa 0.59).
agent_test: Implement prior-art check with facet-based re-rank; measure drop rate on our candidates.

claim: Real feedback beats rating: evolutionary search over LLM ideas with execution outcomes beat best-of-N (GRPO accuracy 69.4% vs human best 68.8%), but RL on one effectiveness reward collapsed diversity (119 of 128 ideas in two patterns) and raised the mean, not the max.
schema_part: S-test / G (verify before commit), S-select (keep tail)
agent_test: Run candidates through a cheap test and keep a diversity reserve; check that the max, not just the mean, improves.

claim: Expert ratings of the same idea drift over time (test-retest ICC 0.59-0.74, 63 researchers, 7,938 ratings); an ideation selector aligned to wave-1 ratings lost its gain after drift was removed.
schema_part: S-select / G (do not trust fixed rating targets)
agent_test: Do not tune a selector on one snapshot of ratings; re-test on held-out later labels.

claim: No study was found that (a) replicates the K&V topic-origination result outside patents, (b) compares tournament, retrieval and past-vs-future selectors on LLM ideas against impact, (c) ablates conventional-plus-atypical seeding, or (d) measures non-NLP execution impact. These stay open.
agent_test: These are tests we would run ourselves.
